    📦 Apps & versions

    The Android (APK) and Windows (EXE / MSI) apps each shop sees under Settings ▸ Install App — only its own app (a Hotel shop never gets the Shop app). A release is offered only once its real file is uploaded and you publish it; size and SHA-256 are measured by the server. Build the files with the GitHub workflows android / windows (Actions ▸ the run ▸ Artifacts). Customers need a SIGNED release APK (add the signing secrets — see native/README.md); a "debug-TEST-ONLY" APK is for testing only.

    🗄️ Databases & cleanup

    Every database the system uses, how full it is, and what can be cleaned up. Only figures the server could really measure are shown; anything else says “not measurable” and why. Sales, payments, stock and customer records are never deleted by cleanup.

    🧹 Database storage

    WhatKept for (days)Archived first
    per D1 database. Free plan: 0.5 GB each (5 GB per account); paid plan: 10 GB each.

    💾 Weekly backups

    💾 Shop data size & safety

    How big every shop's synced data is. Every save has to load the whole shop into memory on the server, so a shop is limited to about 12 MB (a busy shop makes ~1.7 KB per sale). A shop can be moved into its own database (🗄️ button): no size limit, nothing archived away, and tills only ever download a recent window while older history is fetched by date range. Shops that are still a single record archive their own old history automatically once they reach 80% of that limit (keeping the newest 90 days, or fewer if needed), so nobody at a shop ever has to deal with storage; the archives are kept and can be restored or downloaded below. Two manual levers, both reversible: 🗜️ Compress only shrinks the copy kept on disk (lossless; nothing changes for anyone) — it does not lower the size that counts. 🗄️ Archive old history is what actually shrinks a shop: sales, stock movements, expenses… older than N days are moved to a downloadable archive and every device then shows only the recent history until you restore it.

    🔎 SEO management

    Keeps the public site (mydukapos.store) easy for Google to find and understand. These are four different things and this page never mixes them up: found by the site (we serve it) → in the sitemap (we list it) → submitted to Google (you or the API sent the sitemap) → crawled / indexed by Google (only Google decides; shown only when Google is connected). A sitemap helps Google discover pages; it does not guarantee indexing or ranking.

    ↗ Open Google Search Console

    🗺️ Sitemap centre

    NameTypeURLURLsValidationActions
    Loading…

    The whole public site is one sitemap file (17 addresses, far below Google's 50,000-address limit), so there is no sitemap index to submit: submit sitemap.xml. It lists only pages that answer 200, are not marked noindex and use the canonical https://mydukapos.store address. No made-up “last modified” dates are printed.

    📘 Submit to Google Search Console (copy & paste)

    1. Open Google Search Console and choose the mydukapos.store domain property (sc-domain:mydukapos.store).
    2. In the left menu open Indexing → Sitemaps (direct link).
    3. Under “Add a new sitemap” paste sitemap.xml (Google also accepts the full address):
    4. Press Submit. Status “Success” means Google fetched the file; it does not mean the pages are indexed.
    5. Open URL inspection, paste an important page address and read Google's verdict. For a page that is eligible and not yet indexed choose Request indexing.
    6. Come back here, press Run site audit now and fix anything listed below. Re-submitting is only needed after the sitemap's address changes: Google re-reads a submitted sitemap on its own.

    🔗 Google connection (optional)

    Works with whichever printer mode is selected below. With "System print dialog", the dialog still opens once — this just removes the extra "Print Out" tap. For it to be fully silent too, launch Chrome with the --kiosk-printing flag (desktop only). With Bluetooth/USB, it prints straight away with no dialog at all.

    Works with most generic USB thermal receipt printers, straight from the browser — no driver and no print dialog. If it doesn’t show up in the chooser, your printer likely needs a driver and won’t work over WebUSB; use "System print dialog" instead. Needs to be reconnected once per browser session.     📷 Barcode Scanner

    No pairing needed here — nearly all barcode scanners (USB or Bluetooth) act as a keyboard: they "type" the code and press Enter automatically. Just plug it in (or pair it as a Bluetooth keyboard in your device's Bluetooth settings), then scan.

    • On the 🛒 Sales Counter tab: scanning adds the item straight to the cart, from anywhere on the page.
    • On the 📦 Add New Items tab: scanning fills in the barcode, and looks up the product name automatically if it's a recognized product. If the item is already in your inventory, its existing details load so you can edit them.

    Waiting for a scan...

    🗄️ Cash Drawer

    Cash drawers plug into the receipt printer itself (an RJ11/RJ12 port on the back), not into the computer directly — the printer sends it the "kick open" signal. Bluetooth and USB printer modes trigger this directly. "System print dialog" mode can now trigger it too, but only if your printer's driver is set to raw/"Generic / Text Only" mode (most thermal receipt printer drivers can be) — the kick command rides along inside the printed receipt itself. If your drawer doesn't open in that mode, switch the printer's driver to Generic / Text Only, or use Bluetooth/USB instead for guaranteed support.

    🍳 Kitchen Order Tickets

    When a sale includes one or more services, print a plain no-prices ticket for the kitchen — item names and quantities only, in large bold text. Uses the same printer as receipts (system dialog, or a connected Bluetooth/USB printer).

    With "System print dialog", this opens a second print job right after the receipt's — expect two dialogs per sale. With Bluetooth/USB it just prints straight after the receipt with no extra tap.

    🖥️ Customer / Pole Display

    Shows only the running total on a small second screen facing the customer — no login, no other app screens reachable from it. Open it once on this device, drag its window onto the second screen, then press F11 there to go full-screen. It updates live as items are added, and briefly shows the amount tendered and change once a sale completes.

    Works with any small monitor or tablet browser connected to (or mirroring) this device — it's just this same app opened to a second window, not special hardware.

    ❓ Guide

    Quick answers for the parts of this app that trip people up most. Tap a question to expand it.

    💳 How do I get M-Pesa payments actually working?

    You need one of the options, set up under ⚙️ Settings → 💳 Payment Gateway:

    Option A — Safaricom Daraja directly. Needs a Daraja app (Consumer Key/Secret), your Paybill or Till Number, and your Lipa Na M-Pesa Passkey. Use "Till Number" as the transaction type if you take payments on a Till, "Paybill" otherwise. The Callback URL is sent automatically with every request — you only need to copy it somewhere if Safaricom specifically asks you to pre-register one.

    Once saved, the key/credential boxes disappear and are replaced with a green "✅ Payment configured" notice — that's confirmation it saved, not a sign something's hidden from you. There's no way to view a saved key again afterwards (this is deliberate, for security); to change it, use Reset to clear it and enter the new one.

    If more than one is configured at once, the first one set up is used — force one specifically with the "Force a specific provider" dropdown at the bottom of that page.

    🖨️ Which printer mode should I use, and why won't copies/the drawer work?

    System print dialog works with any printer already installed on the device (via USB, network, or Windows/Mac driver) — no pairing needed, but it opens a print preview each time. Bluetooth and USB modes connect directly to a thermal receipt printer and print silently with no dialog at all, once paired/connected in this same Hardware settings page.

    Multiple copies: set the number under "Number of Copies Printed per Receipt" — with System mode, all copies go out as ONE print job (one page per copy), so leave your printer driver's own copy count at 1 or you'll get double the copies you expect.

    Cash drawer: it's the printer, not the computer, that triggers the drawer — it plugs into an RJ11/RJ12 port on the back of the printer. Bluetooth/USB modes trigger it directly. System dialog mode can too, but only if the printer's driver is set to "Generic / Text Only" (raw) mode — most thermal printer drivers support this in their settings.

    Kitchen tickets use whichever printer mode is already selected here — there's currently no support for sending receipts and kitchen tickets to two different physical printers from the same device.

    🖨️ How do I stop the print dialog from popping up every time?

    No website or installed app — this one included — is allowed to print silently on its own. Browsers require a confirmation dialog every time; that's a security rule the browser enforces, not something any app's own code can switch off. Installing MyDukaPOS to the home screen doesn't change this either.

    Two real ways around it:

    Bluetooth or USB thermal printer (Settings → Hardware) — these never open a dialog at all, since they send print data straight to the printer instead of going through the browser's print system. If you have a compatible thermal printer, this is the real fix.

    Launch the browser with the --kiosk-printing flag — the standard trick for silent printing to a normal (non-thermal) printer via System dialog mode. Find the shortcut that installing MyDukaPOS created, right-click → Properties, and add --kiosk-printing (with a space before it) to the end of the Target field. Close every open browser window first, then reopen from that shortcut. It'll auto-print to whichever printer is set as the Windows default, with no dialog and no way to pick a different one from the prompt — set the right default printer in Windows first.

    📦🛠️ What's the difference between an Item and a Service?

    Item — something sold exactly as it is: a bag of rice, a bar of soap. Has its own stock count and shows up in the Sales Counter.

    Service — something you charge for without selling a physical unit: key cutting, delivery, installation. A plain service just has a flat price. Tick "Made from components" to link it to a bill of materials instead: add each item it uses and how much one sale uses (fractions like 1/2 work here), and the app then works out cost-per-sale and how many you can currently do from stock automatically. Tick "This is a bundle" instead to sell several items/services together (e.g. Paint + Brush + Roller) at one price — bundle components can be picked from existing stock (so their own stock is deducted correctly when it sells) or typed freely for something with nothing to track. A service is either component-based or a bundle, never both.

    🧾 Delete Voided Sales Records

    A voided sale or bill in this console's own Daily Sales/Bills is normally kept (struck-through) as an audit trail rather than deleted. This permanently ERASES every already-voided record instead, freeing up the list but breaking that audit trail for good. Only records already marked voided are affected.

    ♻️ Reset Sales & Bills History

    Permanently deletes every sale and open bill recorded in this console — including license-sale entries from 🔗 Generate Link. Client license links themselves are entirely separate and are NOT affected; a client's permanent link keeps working exactly as before. Use this to clear out test/demo entries, or just to tidy up old settled records. This cannot be undone.

    🗑️ Reset Inventory

    Permanently removes every item currently in this console's own local Inventory, on every device. This does not touch client links, sales/bill history, or website content.
